methodological_rigor.justification: The study triangulates clinical ctDNA/WES/RNA-seq data from 30 ReFocus-trial patients with Ba/F3 isogenic models, three PDX models, and structural analyses — a design appropriate for mapping on-target resistance. Resistance definitions (primary vs. acquired) are pre-specified using accepted thresholds (ref. 9, 22), and allelic status was assessed where reads permitted, strengthening polyclonality claims. Statistical treatment is adequate but light: a permutation-based exact test is used for comparing mutation spectra against the Goyal et al. cohort, DESeq2 with Benjamini–Hochberg correction is used for GSEA, but no power calculation, no formal missing-data handling, and only IC50 fold-changes (no CIs) are reported for Ba/F3 assays. Preclinical rigor has gaps: no mention of blinded tumor measurement or randomization in PDX experiments, Mycoplasma testing was skipped (explicitly acknowledged), and PDX replicates (n=6 mice/group) are small. Limitations — genetic-only focus, small sample, inter-panel ctDNA variability, single-mutation PDXs — are candidly acknowledged in the Discussion.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: The design is a prospective-but-small translational case series of 30 patients drawn from a phase I/II trial with convenience post-progression biosampling and a non-randomized historical comparison to Goyal et al.'s futibatinib cohort — best mapped to Oxford LoE 4 (small series/low-quality cohort for the clinical claims). Clinical relevance is high: the work defines a reproducible mutational signature (M538/L618) of lirafugratinib resistance that is actionable because futibatinib retains activity against these variants, and n=3 patients already achieved prolonged response with the proposed sequence. Endpoints are patient-relevant (RECIST response, PFS, disease control) and the findings directly inform near-term precision-oncology sequencing decisions once lirafugratinib is approved (expected 2026–2027). The small n (especially n=3 for the lirafugratinib→futibatinib sequence) and absence of randomized confirmation prevent a higher clinical-relevance score.

reporting_quality.justification: The study is primarily a biomarker/resistance-marker investigation; REMARK is the closest-fitting checklist (with ARRIVE elements relevant to the PDX work and STROBE elements to the cohort). Key items are reported: patient inclusion criteria, assay platforms (three ctDNA panels, WES at 140x, RNA-seq), biomarker definitions (reference transcript explicitly stated), and ethical approvals with trial registration numbers. Gaps include no CONSORT/REMARK flow diagram, no formal reporting of missing data per patient, limited ARRIVE elements for PDX studies (no blinding, randomization, or sample-size justification stated), and multiplicity correction is applied only in GSEA, not in IC50 or mutation-level comparisons. Data/code availability is weak: no mention of deposited raw sequencing data, no code repository for the permutation test or DESeq2 pipeline, and no supplementary methods repository are cited in the manuscript body — justifying a low data-availability score.

novelty_literature.justification: This is the first systematic characterization of resistance to lirafugratinib (an investigational, highly FGFR2-selective irreversible inhibitor), identifying M538I and L618F as novel dominant on-target resistance mutations in 69% of acquired-resistance cases — a pattern distinct from the N550/V565 futibatinib-resistance signature. The direct comparison to Goyal et al.'s 2025 futibatinib cohort to argue inhibitor complementarity, backed by Ba/F3, PDX, structural, and 3-patient clinical validation, represents a genuinely novel integrative contribution that fills a documented gap in sequencing strategies. Novelty is empirical and translational rather than conceptual (polyclonal FGFR2 kinase-domain resistance is itself an established paradigm from refs. 10–13), and some mutations (G584R, L611V, K660S/T, G664E) are flagged as previously unreported. The positioning is honest about building on authors' and others' prior work rather than overclaiming.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is well-organized with a logical flow from cohort description through resistance characterization, cross-inhibitor comparison, functional validation, structural rationale, and clinical sequencing cases. The abstract is quantitatively grounded (30 patients, 69% M538/L618 enrichment, 3-patient sequence vignettes) and accurately previews the paper. Figure captions are informative and standalone-interpretable, with careful annotation (e.g., Figure 1 footnote on patient ST4785 clarifying the FGFR2 driver ambiguity). Minor issues: a few typographic/grammatical slips ("on difference alleles" in Results; "stemmed from molecular and clinical evolution" in Discussion), occasional nested-clause density in the Discussion, and the transcript-nomenclature paragraph could be summarized in a figure footnote rather than repeated across Methods and Discussion.

key_strengths: First systematic resistance landscape for lirafugratinib with a reproducible M538I/L618F signature identified in 69% of acquired-resistance cases
Multi-modal validation: ctDNA + tissue WES/RNA-seq + Ba/F3 isogenic models + 3 PDX models + structural analysis converge on the same conclusion
Clinically actionable: 3 patients already demonstrate prolonged futibatinib response after lirafugratinib progression, directly informing sequencing strategy
Rigorous cross-inhibitor comparison with Goyal et al.'s futibatinib cohort using a permutation test showing complementary (non-overlapping) resistance spectra
Candid acknowledgment of limitations: genetic-only focus, small n, inter-panel ctDNA variability, single-mutation PDXs, intervening therapies
key_concerns: Small sample (n=30 total; only n=3 received the proposed lirafugratinib→futibatinib sequence) limits strength of clinical sequencing recommendation
Historical, non-matched comparison to Goyal et al. for the futibatinib arm introduces selection and platform confounders not fully adjusted for
No power calculation, no CIs on IC50 fold-changes, no blinding/randomization reported for PDX tumor measurement
Weak data/code availability posture — no deposited raw sequencing data or analysis code cited in the manuscript body
Mycoplasma testing not performed on Ba/F3 lines (acknowledged) and PDXs derived from biopsies containing a single kinase-domain mutation each, limiting modeling of polyclonal resistance
chief_reviewer.rationale: A methodologically solid, clinically relevant translational resistance study with clear mechanistic and sequencing implications, but with small n, historical comparator, and modest statistical/reproducibility reporting that keep it below top-tier (Tier 1); best suited to a Tier 2 translational-oncology venue after minor revisions addressing data availability, PDX reporting, and effect-size CIs.
